sentences.text: Hydrolagus is a genus of marine fish found in the Atlantic, Indian, and Pacific Oceans, containing 22 recognized species such as the spotted ratfish and African chimaera.
These animals have an unusual appearance featuring pectoral fins that resemble wings, a dorsal fin ending in a point, and a long whip-like tail.
The oldest fossil record of this genus dates to the Miocene epoch.
The genus was formally described by T. N. Gill in 1862.
This group has undergone no changes in the last 150 million years.
Some species live at depths of 736 meters in total darkness, detecting electromagnetic radiation from other marine creatures using specialized nerves on the sides of their bodies.

Taxonomically, Hydrolagus belongs to the kingdom Animalia, the phylum Chordata, the subphylum Vertebrata, the infraphylum Gnathostomata, the subclass Holocephali, the order Chimaeriformes, and the class Chondrichthyes.
It is classified within the family Chimaeridae, which serves as its parent group.
Fossil remains are known from the Miocene and Pliocene periods of California.
